text.p: Swiss shares gained more than one percent on Tuesday as better-than-expected U.S. consumer price data and Wall Street's firm opening pushed prices higher, dealers said.
The broad SPI rose 28.84 to end at 2,935.72 and the blue-chip SMI was up 57.1, or 1.25 percent, to 4,643.4.
U.S. consumer prices moved up by a modest 0.1 percent in March after rising 0.3 percent in February.
Roche, which led the actives list, slid 80 Swiss francs to 11,850 after the market showed some disappointment with the pharmaceutical group's first-quarter sales figures.
Novartis, second on the actives list, rose 25 to 1,785.
Total trade volume was 2.34 billion Swiss francs.

Roche said at its annual news conference today that sales in the first quarter of 1997 rose by 18 percent in Swiss francs but by only 3.0 percent in local currencies. Dealers said the low local currency growth rate, in pharmaceuticals in particular, had disappointed the market.
Nestle firmed along with the market, adding 23 to close at 1,740. Other blue-chips also showed solid gains. Swiss Re gained 29 to end at 1,552.
Holderbank closed nine francs higher at 1,137.
After the market closed the cement group said its 1996 profit after an extraordinary provision of 450 million francs but before minorities fell to 196 million francs after 611 million francs in 1995.
The net profit after minorities was down to 43 million francs from a prior 450 million.
